content.title: About
content.content: Avocado is the edible fruit of the avocado tree (Persea americana), native to Central and South America and now cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. The fruit has a creamy texture, a mild buttery flavor, and is rich in healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Avocado is sometimes called the "fruit butter" because of its smooth texture.
It contains more monounsaturated fat than olive oil.
Inside each fruit is a large seed that can be roasted and eaten.
One avocado provides over 10% of the daily recommended potassium intake.
There are more than 500 avocado varieties, with Hass being the most common.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: These fats help lower LDL cholesterol and support heart health.

items.title: High potassium content
items.content: Potassium aids blood pressure regulation and muscle‑nerve function.

items.title: Source of vitamins E and C
items.content: Antioxidant vitamins protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to avocado.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite its benefits, avocado is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs may experience discomfort when consuming large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Avocado is eaten raw: sliced into salads, spread on toast, blended into smoothies, used in guacamole, or as a mayo substitute. A ripe fruit yields to gentle pressure; if it’s too firm, let it ripen at room temperature.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unripe avocados at room temperature until they soften. Once ripe, store them in the refrigerator for up to 3–5 days. To slow browning, drizzle cut pieces with lemon juice.
